subject.title: fix(plugins): preserve already-loaded plugins across scoped harness activation

question: Should scoped harness activation use a request-scoped registry handle, or should the plugin loader gain a transactional merge that preserves existing registry objects while adding the missing owner?
rationale: Both approaches can prevent eviction, but the permanent ownership and lifecycle semantics affect plugin registration, pinned surfaces, cleanup, and concurrent runtime users; the current broad reload is not a safe default.

options.title: Use a request-scoped handle
options.body: Load or resolve the missing harness owner for this operation without replacing or rebuilding the process-global active registry.

options.title: Add transactional registry merging
options.body: Teach the registry-loader boundary to retain existing registrations and merge only newly required plugin surfaces with explicit cleanup and collision tests.

options.title: Accept broad reload semantics
options.body: Keep the current design only if owners explicitly require all active plugins to be reloaded and add idempotence, service-lifecycle, concurrency, and live-runtime proof.

recommendation.title: Use a request-scoped handle
recommendation.body: Load or resolve the missing harness owner for this operation without replacing or rebuilding the process-global active registry.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history directly connects this person to provider-owned harness activation and its tests.
